notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP). Plain curl was blocked by PerimeterX (px-captcha, homepage returned 'Access to this page has been denied'). robots.txt has no Claude/Anthropic-specific disallow, so proceeded; switched to curl_cffi with Chrome-TLS impersonation (still tier-1 direct HTTP fetch, not a proxy/reader), which reliably returned full SSR HTML (900KB-2.2MB) for every URL fetched, so tier 2/3 were not needed (Playwright with plain Chromium was tried once and was also PerimeterX-blocked, confirming curl_cffi was the correct tier-1 path). Investigated Birch Lane's own taxonomy independently (did not assume it mirrors AllModern/Joss & Main): fetched seo-category sitemap (bl_sitemap_cat0.xml), the mega-menu embedded in every page's RSC payload, and the 'Holiday' hub page (/holiday/cat/holiday-c1837548.html) plus every child link found on it. Confirmed via full nav link scan for keywords (valentine, diwali, hanukkah, new-year, st-patrick, mardi-gras, july-4/independence, lunar-new-year, ramadan, eid, kwanzaa) that Birch Lane has NO categories for Valentine's Day, Diwali, Hanukkah, New Year, or any other festival beyond Christmas/Halloween/Easter/Thanksgiving/generic 'Holiday' - these terms produced zero nav links across all fetched pages. 'Holiday' is a real top-level nav parent (own URL, c1837548) whose own page has no pagination and functions purely as a hub linking to Christmas/Halloween/Easter/Thanksgiving plus 5 cross-holiday subcategories (Decorative Accents, Garlands & Swags, Lighting, Storage, Wreaths) - kept as a grouping row (is_group, qty null) per the parent/child rule, since counting it would double-count its children. Excluded 3 '/curated/' pages found in the nav ("Company's Coming: Halloween", "Company's Coming: Christmas", "Thanksgiving Hosting & Decor") as editorial/gift-guide landing pages, not real PLPs (no pagination, no product grid/count of their own). For Christmas/Halloween/Easter/Thanksgiving (each a genuine paginated PLP with ?curpage=N links), qty was read from the structured GraphQL cache embedded in the page's Next.js RSC payload: BlockBuilderCoreListingCollection.collection(BrowseByEntityListingCollection).listingsConnection.pageInfo.totalCount - the single listing-collection instance on each page, wired to the page's 'Shop All' heading + BrowseResultCount widget (verified same JSON shape/position on all 4 pages, immediately after 6 SSR-rendered product cards' own review totalCount fields). Spot-verified this method is not an over-count: Halloween's totalCount=286 is consistent with its confirmed page structure (48 items/page grid, deep curpage pagination that reveals further pages via a sliding pagination window as you page forward - curpage=5 revealed curpage=7, etc. - matching an order of magnitude in the hundreds, not the 6-per-curpage superficially visible on page 1, which is an SSR lazy-load artifact). For the 5 generic Holiday subcategories (true 48-item/page grids, no visible on-page results-count text, and no equivalent totalCount field present in their RSC payload), qty was obtained by full enumeration: fetched every ?curpage=N via curl_cffi until an empty page was returned, counting unique product PDP ids per page (48/page standard; final page's count, full or partial, immediately followed by an empty page, gives the true end) - Decorative Accents: pages 1-10 all full (48) then page 11 empty = 480; Garlands & Swags: pages 1-9 full (48) then page 10=46 (partial) then page 11 empty = 478; Lighting: pages 1-2 full (48) then page 3=26 (partial, no further curpage link) = 122; Storage: single page, no pagination links = 23; Wreaths: pages 1-5 full (48) then page 6=36 (partial, no further curpage link) = 276. Christmas itself additionally links to 5 of its own Christmas-specific sb0 subcategories (Christmas Trees, Ornaments & Tree Toppers, Outdoor Christmas Decorations, Stockings & Stocking Holders, Tree Skirts) - these were left unenumerated and un-listed since Christmas's own 'Shop All' total (1192) already aggregates them; listing both would double-count. No zero-result internal search was used to conclude absence anywhere - absence of other festivals was established via exhaustive nav/link scanning across 9 fetched pages, not search.
